reports.title: Jasbir Pahal: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Calderdale Royal Hospital (CRH), the hospital with a hyper-acute stroke unit closest to Jasbir's home address, does not offer a thrombectomy service, whether in or out of hours.
concerns.hazard: lack of thrombectomy service at CRH

concerns.quote: Thrombectomy is a time-sensitive procedure, requiring to be performed within six hours of the onset of stroke symptoms to have its best chance of being successful, although it can be performed outside of that timeframe if investigative imaging suggests it may still be effective.

Anyone whose nearest hyper-acute stroke unit is at a district general hospital in West Yorkshire and who suffers a stroke outside of those hours during the week, or between 1500 hrs on a Friday and 0800 hrs the following Monday, does not have access to a thrombectomy service.

It is undesirable that patients such as Jasbir should be subject to the vagaries of local arrangements when they are in urgent need of potentially life-saving treatment, and that they should be denied access to such treatment simply by reason of their home address.
concerns.hazard: geographic inequity in stroke treatment access

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of a 24/7 thrombectomy service for stroke patients in their respective regions. The earlier report focuses on Cornwall, while the later report notes a broader gap across the South West.
links.earlier_quote: There is no thrombectomy service available 24/7 for RCHT patients.
links.later_quote: there is a gap in the availability of the time critical and potentially lifesaving thrombectomy emergency procedure to patients that have suffered a severe stroke in the South West

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that patients cannot receive thrombectomy services outside regular daytime hours due to limited provision or funding. The earlier report cites restricted operating hours; the later report cites insufficient funding for overnight service.
links.earlier_quote: Anyone whose nearest hyper-acute stroke unit is at a district general hospital in West Yorkshire and who suffers a stroke outside of those hours during the week, or between 1500 hrs on a Friday and 0800 hrs the following Monday, does not have access to a thrombectomy service.
links.later_quote: The court heard there is insufficient funding in place for patients to be provided with an urgent mechanical thrombectomy between the hours of 4 pm and 8 am at University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that thrombectomy services are not reliably available outside normal working hours, leading to missed treatment opportunities. The earlier report cites a complete lack of 24/7 provision in Cornwall, while the later report points to insufficient funding limiting service to 4 pm–8 am at a Sussex trust.
links.earlier_quote: Over the last year it is estimated that 75 stroke patients in Cornwall who would otherwise be suitable for thrombectomy procedures did not receive this procedure because it is not available 24/7 in Cornwall
links.later_quote: The court heard there is insufficient funding in place for patients to be provided with an urgent mechanical thrombectomy between the hours of 4 pm and 8 am at University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust.
